newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 30.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Renegade Karens have launched cross-border raids and burnt down two refugee camps, leaving about 10,000 Karen refugees homeless. A Thai villager and a renegade trooper have been killed in the attack. Their attempt to destroy a third refugee camp in Tha Song Yang district was foiled after the 300-strong raiding force was intercepted by Thai border patrol police. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- Chart Pattana Party has tried to block the Nong Ngu Hao project after a company linked to its secretary-general lost a multi-million-baht landfill contract, says the Social Action Party. The project was suspended after Prayoonvis Co lost the contract at the site of Bangkok's second international airport in Samut Prakan province. (BANGKOK POST)

- The historic legal battle between former prime minister Anand Panyarachun and a retired senior judge, fallout from the infamous judicial crisis, comes to a conclusion tomorrow when the Criminal Court rules whether Anand is guilty of malfeasance, an offence punishable by fine or imprisonment. Supporters of the former premier, calling themselves "Friends of Anand", are expected to gather in strength at the court compound as they did at the start of the hearings in 1993. (THE NATION) + + + +

- At least 10 mega-development projects, including an expressway in Bangkok, are likely to be suspended or delayed as part of the government's move to cut the budget by 100 billion baht over the next two fiscal years. The list has been compiled by the National Economic and Social Development Board, the planning agency, and will be presented shortly to Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan. (THE NATION)

- Thailand has entered into a New Agreement to Borrow (NAB) with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to contribute to a $48 billion international loan source, says Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan. Member countries can borrow from the fund without preconditions in the event of liquidity problems. As a member, Thailand will contribute $490 million. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Petroleum Authority of Thailand has decided to delay its upstream National Petrochemical Corporation (NPC) III project indefinitely, due to an expected oversupply in the market, but will adhere to the original schedule for its downstream project. According to the original plan, the cracker unit should churn out 600,000 tonnes of ethylene and 121,000 tonnes of propylene from 2000. (THE NATION)
